title: VUA release.openForHandoff (v0.1)
description: Tasked command face of the official-SDK upload handoff (proposal 023, M7 row 'Inspection/Release pages and the official SDK handoff'). FROZEN v0.1 (core freeze batch 2026-09-16): freeze hard-precondition 1 closed with both stances on record — the desktop stance (proposal 023 inline 'stance (desktop)' section, 469ef5c via the 52nd-wave merge d73fa10) ruled direction a the action authority with direction b's receipt shape folded into this command's result document (no separate release.handoffBundle command face), and the production stance (proposal 023 inline 'stance (production)' section, wt-4 tree, five points on record) pinned the mechanism facts: the Bridge command face presumes an already-open project, so openForHandoff is editor-process lifecycle management living in the process/window domain — unity-bridge v3 gains zero operations (evolution clause not triggered, hard precondition 5 vacuous), tasking is the unified task nine-state single form, and the freeze batch sets no new real-machine precondition (ruling 15 local-first evidence reusable at W25). Handoff semantics (product boundary, restated): hand the user to the START of the official SDK flow — the upload itself never enters VUA; the result document carries no upload-status field (honesty rules 1/2 pinned by shape; the negative vector pins it). Params are a closed single-key set {buildId} (core freeze ruling, amending the 023 section-3 draft 'buildId + project identity'): the build record is the authoritative project identity (projectId travels on the frozen build-record face), so repeating project identity in params would create a dual-source reconciliation face with zero gain — the desktop stance 'the authoritative identity lives on the build-record face' taken to its conclusion; disagreement reopens the proposal thread. Editor identity resolution (semantic ordering, implementation-owned): explicit injection (021 assembly-face selection authority) first, then the build record's carried editor identity (unityEditorVersion/projectId — the production stance's default, guarding against version-mismatch upgrade side effects), else the typed error vua.release_handoff.editor_unresolved whose diagnosis reuses the environment.verifyEditor semantics (never a new vocabulary). Completion judgment: the Bridge handshake arrival (001 chain) — 'process started' is never a completion judgment; timeout fails honestly (timeout class, inspect_required semantics — never a guessed panel state); OS window focus is best-effort and enters neither the completion judgment nor the receipt facts. Tasking: the unified task nine-state single form (production stance 3); the acceptance reply follows the tasked-command face (inspection.requestRun precedent): poll the application task face by taskId; the succeeded task snapshot's result carries the handoff fact document. storedPath discipline (authority anchor 6): artifact physical paths never appear — project paths and artifact paths are not wire facts; the editor executable identity (exePath/version) is already a frozen editor-verify v0.1 fact family and travels as identity, not as a storage path. Vocabulary family ruling: release.* is the product-action face (actions performed on a build outcome), record.* stays the record read/write face — no overlap (production stance 5, core ruling adopted). Routing-not-wired semantics: the honest absence code vua.release_handoff.unavailable is reserved for the unwired route (the production-domain process/window port and the core use case land in a later slice) and is never folded into a fabricated acceptance or a guessed handoff fact.

buildId.description: The build-record identity handed off (frozen build-record v0.3 face; the same identity family record.get serves). The closed params set: the build record is the single authoritative source for the project identity, so no project field repeats here.

errorCode.description: Closed four-code typed error set (vua.release_handoff.* family). unavailable: the route or the production-domain port is not wired — honest absence, never a fabricated acceptance. invalid_params: params closed-set violations (a shape violation is never folded into an absence). build_unknown: the buildId has no corresponding build record (checked at acceptance time). editor_unresolved: editor identity failed to resolve (no explicit injection and no usable build-record identity); the diagnosis reuses the environment.verifyEditor semantics. Later-phase failures inside the running task (handshake timeout and the like) travel the ordinary task face nine states, not this set.

release-openForHandoffAccepted.description: Tasked-command acceptance (inspection.requestRun reply shape): poll the application task face by taskId; do not poll this method again. The succeeded task snapshot's result carries the handoff fact document (the #22/020 result-reflux channel).

release-openForHandoffFact.description: The handoff fact document (the succeeded task snapshot's result payload): the VUA-side terminal state of the handoff. Carries buildId (direction b's receipt shape folded in per the desktop stance), the project identity resolved from the build record, the editor identity facts (identity, not storage paths), and the occurrence instant. additionalProperties false pins honesty rules 1/2 by shape: there is no upload-status field — the upload happens in the official SDK and is never a VUA fact to guess at.

buildId.description: The handed-off build identity (the SDK-side cross-check anchor).

projectId.description: Project identity resolved from the build record (authoritative identity face; never a filesystem path — storedPath discipline).

editor.description: The editor identity the handoff targeted (identity facts only; exePath is the frozen editor-verify v0.1 fact family, not an artifact storage path).

exePath.description: The editor executable identity (editor-verify v0.1 fact family).

version.description: The editor version string (display form, as the verification face established it).

occurredAt.description: The instant the handoff completed (RFC 3339), the VUA-side terminal-state fact.
